summary: Revise at 6.0 (Caiman 7, ship 7.5). At 300 px the ring reads as a rose because it has prickles, an open bloom and a hip. It does not yet look like a Kings of Alchemy piece. Every blocking gate is green and checked against report.json and verification.json. The lost-wax wall census gate is recorded as FAILED: on the export build, 5 real walls of 0.02 mm² or more lie between 0.05 and 0.8 mm, as thin as 0.054 and 0.083 mm. The author marked it non-blocking, but review.md makes any recorded failed gate an automatic revise. On the art side, the bloom is 22 cookie-cutter petals with vertical extruded walls and a crumpled-foil noise skin, stacked round a plain collet whose smooth rim still shows. There is no spiral and no reflexed, drooping outer petal, so it reads as a generic gem flower that happens to be withered. The hip is the weakest part. It is a tall plain cylindrical can with five round pipe-bends cut off flat, which reads as a beetle or a spider, not a dried rose hip. Its garnet renders faceted and banded, and almost the same raspberry as the ruby. The leaf's leaflets are flat slabs with stair-stepped serrations, and the rachis ends in a flat-cut tube. The ten prickles are blunt slug-shaped pegs that barely grade (scale 1.0 to 0.8). They run to θ 338° and 216°, into the lower third of the band. The bypass crossing, the ring's structural idea, is hidden under the bloom. The rest of the band is a bare round stem, well below Caiman's density. A concrete round can fix the hip, the bloom's construction and the census walls, so revise.
strengths: Names the rose at 300 px without a caption: thorns, an open bloom and a hip together (hero-300, face-300, contact-300).
Clear large / medium / small hierarchy in the face view: the bloom about 13 mm, the hip about 8 mm, the leaf and prickles small. The ruby heart is a strong focal point.
One theme from face to palm: bloom and hip on the face, prickles on the shoulders, a plain stem at the palm (palm.png). Nothing scattered.
Bloom built as 4 petal rings (22 petals), so the head has real depth and casts shadow in hero and side, not low relief.

Every blocking gate green with clean numbers: 0 degenerates and 0 crossings on the ring, the pattern and all 34 made parts, notes empty, 0 DFM, 2/2 stones, 0 metal in stones, thinnest field wall 2.01 mm, 1.29 M triangles, cold reload identical, 1 design.set patch, template 296 KB under the 300 KB procedural budget.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Bloom and hip on the face, prickles on both shoulders, plain stem at the palm and a smooth bore (palm.png, reverse.png). Everything belongs to the one rose stem.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and face-300 name a rose through thorns, an open flower and a hip together. Marginal pass: cover the prickles and the bloom alone reads as a camellia or peony. The hip reads as a stone in a spidery can, so the read rests on the prickles.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: In leaf-close all three leaflets have stair-stepped serrated rims and flat slab faces. In bloom-close the petal rims are faceted polylines over vertical extruded walls, and the procedural crumple noise smears the petal faces into foil. stamps.count is 0: nothing is struck with a true outline.

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings, visible, coloured as the plant's fruit or buds
checklist.reason: Both stones sit in made bezels and are visible. But the hip's collet (hip-close) is a tall plain cylinder with a dark gap under its base, and its five sepals are round pipe-bends with flat cut ends that pierce the collet rim. The garnet renders as a banded, faceted cone, not a smooth cabochon. In face and stones it looks the same raspberry as the ruby, not the dark wine of a dried hip. The heart collet's plain rim still shows round the ruby (bloom-close).

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The petals are extruded profiles with vertical side walls. The leaflets are flat slabs. The hip collet is a turned cylinder with a stepped disc underneath (palm.png). The sepals are constant-section pipes. reverse.png shows a flat-cut stepped stub where arm B's tip ends near 5 o'clock.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable: a procedural Bypass HighDome round stem, no factory stock.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: No other Vepres ring is built yet. The off-centre bloom-and-hip top with side prickles is unlike any planned signet or vine. The bypass crossing that should make it unique is hidden under the bloom (bare-vs-finished): the finished ring reads as a closed round band.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The face is dense, but from about θ 230° to 330° the band is a bare polished tube. The prickles are blunt pegs of near-uniform size, with no hook and no broad base. Caiman carries worked surface over its whole visible body. This ring carries it over about a third.

punch_list.zone: Hip on arm B, θ 38°: 'Hip collet' (#5), 'Hip's dried sepal' (#19) / 'Hip's dried crown' (#20), 'Hip body' (#21), garnet
punch_list.change: Rebuild the hip as a fruit, not a stone in a can. Make 'Hip body' an urn (the ring_local_outlines urn profile) about 7 mm tall that swells from a 2.5 mm neck at the stem to 7.4 mm and closes over the garnet's girdle as its own collet. Drop the separate cylinder or cut it to 0.6 mm above the girdle, hidden inside the urn lip. Replace the five round pipe wisps with flat lens-section sepals 0.7 x 0.5 mm, as the plan says: twisted 60°, tapering to a point at end_scale 0.4 (no flat cut end), springing from the urn lip and arching 1.0-1.5 mm over the dome's shoulder before curling outward. Seat the urn base into the arm with a 0.4 mm blend bead so no gap shows. Retint the garnet darker and browner than the ruby (about sRGB [0.28, 0.03, 0.05]), and tessellate the cabochon reference mesh finely enough to render a smooth dome.
punch_list.acceptance: In hip-close no vertical cylinder wall shows above the stem: an urn swells from the neck to the stone. All 5 sepals end in points, none pierces a rim, and no dark gap shows under the base. The garnet dome shows no faceting bands. In face-300 the hip and ruby read as two different reds, and covering the bloom the hip alone reads as a rose hip.

punch_list.change: Sculpt the petals instead of extruding them. Build each petal as a lofted or swept cupped shell, thick at the base (at least 0.9 mm) and tapering to a 0.5 mm rounded rim, with no vertical side wall. Turn ring 1 (3-4 petals) into an overlapping spiral wrap that rises 1.5 mm over the collet rim, so no smooth collet metal shows round the ruby. Rotate each ring 1-3 petals so they overlap in one direction. Reflex ring 4 outward and down 20-35° below the bloom plane, with curled-back tips. Replace the high-frequency crumple noise with 2-3 broad dried folds per petal (wavelength at least 1.5 mm, amplitude at most 0.3 mm), so withering reads as curl, not foil.
punch_list.acceptance: In bloom-close no petal shows a vertical extruded edge or faceted rim. No collet rim shows round the ruby. The inner petals visibly spiral one way. In side.png the outer row droops below the inner rows. Covering the prickles and hip in face-300, the head alone reads as a rose.

punch_list.change: Find the part at each real-wall point. The first two lie on the bloom's lower petals over arm A, the next two in the upper petal rings, and the fifth at the stem's side near θ 180°. Thicken or fuse each to at least 0.8 mm across, or merge the overlapping petal pairs so no 0.05-0.8 mm sliver remains between them. Give every petal and leaflet rim the 0.5 mm rounded edge from item 2, so the edge census no longer reports near-0 mm knife rims.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json wall_census.real_walls is empty on both the export and draft builds, and the census gate reads pass: true. The other gates stay green: field Castable, thinnest wall at least 0.8 mm, 0 crossings on every part.

punch_list.zone: Leaf on arm A beside the bloom: 'Leaf, terminal / upper lateral / lower lateral leaflet' (#22-#24), 'Leaf, rachis' (#25)
punch_list.change: Rebuild the leaflets as cupped lofts with the plan's five lens sections (widths 0.6 / 1.9 / 2.2 / 1.4 / 0.5, turned up to 35°), not flat slabs. Cut the serration as a smooth closed outline: 9-12 teeth per side, 0.25 mm deep, sampled at least 8 points per tooth so no step shows. Add a sunken midrib 0.15 mm deep. Run the rachis into the stem with a blended petiole base, not a flat-cut tube end lying beside the band.
punch_list.acceptance: In leaf-close every leaflet rim is a smooth toothed curve with no stair-steps, and each leaflet shows a cup and a midrib. The rachis has no flat cut end. In face-300 the leaf reads as a compound rose leaf.

punch_list.change: Reshape each prickle as a rose prickle: a broad elongated base about 2.0 x 1.2 mm along the stem, tapering to a fine point (tip radius at most 0.15 mm) that hooks down the stem by 30-40°. Replace the blunt peg. Grade them strongly, scale 1.0 to 0.5. Move them up the shoulders: arm A from θ 60° to 10°, arm B from θ 130° to 170°, so the lower third of the band (θ 200-340°) is plain stem.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png and hero.png each prickle shows a broad base, a sharp hooked point and a visible size grade. In hero-300 and side.png no prickle sits below the band's horizontal midline.

punch_list.zone: Band, arm crossing at about θ 60-120° and arm tips; plain stem θ 230-330°
punch_list.change: Make the bypass legible. Open 1.0-1.5 mm of visible air between arm A and arm B where they pass under the bloom and hip, so the crossing shows in side.png. Finish arm B's tip near 5 o'clock (the stepped stub in reverse.png) with a rounded cut-cane end or a node. Add low growth nodes and fine longitudinal stem striations (0.08-0.12 mm) along the plain stem, so it reads as a rose cane and not a polished tube, while staying plain of motifs.
punch_list.acceptance: In side.png and bare-vs-finished the two arms show as separate stems passing each other. reverse.png shows no flat-cut stepped stub. In hero.png the palm-side band shows cane texture but no motifs.
